comment: The table of the lint of the audit rows of D9.8 in tools/fort_lint.py: the declaration row of
each `extern fn` of a trusted module (present, once, its symbol, the five words of A7 once in
any case, below the `///` text), the call rows of a function (present, the count of each
callee as the body spells it, white space, ranges and members included, and a call through
each kind of function value), a boundary function as a value only on its way to C, the reach
of a boundary function, and the trust of a module by its root or by `import extern;`. Each row
breaks one part. The source is the product, so the build does nothing and the md5 guard reads
tools/fort_lint.py. The stage runs test/fort_lint_rows_test.py, whose reach tests compare the
lint with the compiler. The table runs in the VM with the debug preset after `tools/vm build`.
The rows D9.8-lang-* break the checks of the files of test/lang: D9.8 only, with the
`--cfg` options of the `//! flags:` directive of their test. The rows D9.8-cite-* break the check
of a citation of the row of a fort function, and D9.8-mut-global-* the check of a `mut` global.
D9.8-mut-global-literal and -enclosing break the search for the call that holds the name, and
D9.8-cite-body, -extern, -extern-body, -extern-path and -trusted the callee that a citation
may name. The rows D9.8-group-* break the one reader of a callee, `call_callee`, and each place
that takes a callee from it through a group, `(strlen)(p)`. The text count reads a callee
through that reader too, so the range rule of the text is the row D9.8-callee-range.
The rows D9.8-cite-wrap, -wrap-callee and -capital break a form of a citation that the lint
accepts. D9.8-cite-start-*, -unread, -group and -callee-name break the rule that text that
starts a citation reads as one or is a problem. D9.8-keyword-* and D9.8-compiler-form break
the rule that a keyword and a compiler form are the callee of no call. D9.8-group-argument and
-argument-each break an argument in a group, `take_cb((takep))`, and D9.8-group-alone a name
in the list of a `cast`.
The rows D9.8-refused-* break the check of the 15 names that no row makes legal ("One
thread", "Calls from C"). One row for each name puts another name in its place:
D9.8-refused-pthread-create, -clone, -clone3, -thrd-create, -vfork, -setjmp, -u-setjmp,
-sigsetjmp, -uu-sigsetjmp, -getcontext, -longjmp, -u-longjmp, -siglongjmp, -setcontext and
-swapcontext. In a row name, `u` stands for one `_` at the start of the C name. The other
rows break the files that get the check (-check, -lang, -trusted), the text that is a
declaration (-comment, -word, -space, -longer, -suffix, -each) and the problem (-line,
-column, -reason, -vfork-reason).
The rows D2.1-no-utf8-* break the report of a file with a byte that is no UTF-8 text: the
problem, its line and its byte column, the other checks of that file, and the read of the
`//! flags:` of a main.ft. D9.8-cite-number, -unread-* and -cut* break the message of a
number in a group, of text that does not read as a citation, and of a citation that a line
end cuts inside a module path. D2.1-line-end breaks the line ends of the text of a file.
The rows D9.8-gives-* break the check of the `// gives:` line of a function of a trusted
module. -check and -word break the report, and -column breaks its place. -line-start,
-space, -text and -text-space break the form of a row line. -first-item breaks the row of a
function that is not first on its line. -pointer, -span, -string, -group, -fn-parameter,
-fn-result and -own-type break the types that ask for the line. -struct, -struct-depth,
-field-byte and -field-last break the reach through the structs of each module.
-result-start, -result-list and -result-open break the place of the result type.

a line separator or a paragraph separator, U+2028 or U+2029, is text of a row line
a lone `\r` ends a line of the check, and the lexer counts `\n` only
